title: [Forests] Forest-Type Stratification Outperforms Hyperparameter Optimization for ICESat-2-Based Carbon Stock Estimation in Subtropical Forests
abstract: An accurate estimation of forest carbon stocks is essential for understanding the terrestrial carbon cycle and supporting climate change mitigation. ICESat-2 LiDAR provides globally consistent canopy structure information, but its application in heterogeneous subtropical forests remains challenging due to forest-type heterogeneity and the risk of optimistic accuracy estimates from inappropriate validation. This study aims to quantify the relative contributions of forest-type stratification and hyperparameter optimization to ICESat-2-based carbon stock estimation. Using Hangzhou, China, as a case study, we derived reference carbon densities from 2019 Forest Resource Inventory sub-compartments and matched each sub-compartment with the nearest ICESat-2 ATL08 segment. A three-stage modeling framework was designed using Random Forest: (A) global model with fixed hyperparameters; (B) global model with hyperparameters optimized via Optuna; and (C) forest-type-specific models using the same optimized hyperparameters. A nested cross-validation (fivefold outer, twofold inner) with paired validation samples was employed to prevent data leakage and ensure fair comparison. Results showed that forest-type stratification was the dominant driver of accuracy improvement, whereas global hyperparameter optimization provided only marginal gains. For mixed forest and evergreen broadleaf forest, type-specific models increased R2 from 0.34 to 0.63 and from 0.45 to 0.69, respectively. For bamboo forest, the global model completely failed (R2 < 0), while the type-specific model achieved R2 = 0.44 and reduced RMSE from 22.0 to 3.2 Mg C/ha. These findings demonstrate that in heterogeneous subtropical forests, stratifying by forest type should be prioritized over exhaustive hyperparameter tuning for ICESat-2-based carbon stock estimation.

title: [Remote Sensing] UAV-LiDAR and Machine Learning for Estimating Individual Tree Diameter at Breast Height in Chinese Fir Plantations Approaching Maturity
abstract: Chinese fir (Cunninghamia lanceolata) is a major plantation species in southern China, and diameter at breast height (DBH) is an essential variable for forest inventory, biomass estimation, and carbon accounting. However, direct DBH extraction from UAV-LiDAR is limited in near-mature stands because lower-stem points are often occluded by dense canopies. This study developed a UAV-LiDAR-based workflow for individual tree segmentation, structural parameter extraction, and multivariate DBH estimation in near-mature Chinese fir plantations. Field measurements were conducted in 16 sample plots. Segmentation was evaluated against a common reference set of 428 field trees across the three CHM configurations, and 412 trees with unambiguous one-to-one field-to-crown matches were retained for DBH modeling. Canopy height models (CHMs) with spatial resolutions of 0.5, 0.25, and 0.1 m were compared using watershed segmentation. For the selected 0.25 m CHM, maximum crown-polygon height (CHM_H) and equivalent-area crown diameter (CD) were extracted. CD was calculated from crown area (CA), and CA was therefore excluded from all final multivariate models to avoid deterministic redundancy. Among the tested resolution-smoothing configurations, the 0.25 m CHM yielded the highest recall, precision, and F-score values of 94.86%, 92.69%, and 93.76%, respectively. In the height-metric comparison, CHM_H achieved R2 = 0.802 and RMSE = 0.928 m, slightly outperforming H90 under the prespecified RMSE criterion. On the same holdout, classical height–crown allometry yielded R2 = 0.605, RMSE = 1.701 cm, and MAE = 1.297 cm. BPNN retained the highest reported validation R2 (0.662) and the lowest reported RMSE (1.581 cm) and was selected as the best-performing model under the study design. The workflow provides a practical basis for non-destructive DBH estimation and precision inventory in near-mature Chinese fir plantations.

title: [Remote Sensing] LD-DETR: A Multi-Scale Landslide Detection and Segmentation Network for Complex Geological Environments
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards. High-resolution remote sensing imagery provides an effective means for landslide detection and mapping, supporting geological hazard assessment and early warning. However, existing methods still face challenges in complex mountainous scenes with heterogeneous land cover and geological conditions. These challenges include irregular segmentation boundaries caused by diverse landslide shapes, small-scale detection difficulties due to background interference, and foreground–background class imbalance that hinders effective model optimization. To address these issues, we propose LD-DETR, a network for landslide detection and segmentation. An Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module is integrated into the segmentation head to improve multi-scale feature representation, enabling better segmentation of landslides with varying spatial sizes. To alleviate class imbalance caused by the dominance of non-landslide pixels, a weighted Tversky Loss is introduced to improve the learning of hard samples. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is further combined with orientation-aware data augmentation to enable parameter-efficient adaptation, reducing the proportion of trainable parameters of LD-DETR to 41.07% while keeping the pre-trained backbone parameters frozen. Experiments on the Bijie and Luding Landslide Dataset (BLLD) demonstrate that LD-DETR is competitive with the baseline model and several YOLO-based approaches. The proposed method achieves an F1-score of 95.18% and a Recall of 95%, while the segmentation task reaches an mAP of 59.28%, slightly higher than the RF-DETR baseline. Furthermore, a limited-sample adaptation experiment on the Jiuzhai landslide dataset demonstrates the transferability of the proposed method across different geographic regions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides competitive landslide detection and segmentation performance and offers an approach for fine-grained landslide mapping using remote sensing imagery.

title: [Forests] Bibliometric Analysis of Remote Sensing and GIS Applications for Natural Resource Management in Forest Ecosystems
abstract: Sustainable management of natural resources requires tools that enable a comprehensive analysis of patterns of use, change and conservation of ecosystems. In this context, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing (RS) have established themselves as key technologies for analyzing and promoting the sustainable management of forest ecosystems and other natural resources. This study aimed to analyze the evolution, structure, and trends in scientific output regarding the use of GIS and remote sensing in natural resource management, with an emphasis on forest management, during the period from 1985 to 2025. A systematic bibliometric analysis was conducted using Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, with the literature identification and selection process reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, yielding a final dataset of 679 documents. The results show sustained growth (5% annually), with an increase in citations. The output is concentrated in specialized journals and countries such as the United States and China. From a thematic perspective, the studies focus on forest ecosystems (81%), with a predominance of raster data use (91%). It is concluded that the research field is expanding, with significant advances since the year 2000, consolidating itself as a key area for the monitoring and sustainable management of forest resources. Likewise, the predominance of raster data use reflects an orientation toward large-scale spatial analyses, supported by open-access remote sensing platforms with continuous spatial coverage.

title: [Remote Sensing] Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Multi-Location ABL Wind Profiling with Minimal Instrumentation
abstract: The vertical wind profile within the Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL) is a critical variable for a wide range of applications, including wind energy, air traffic and Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) management, pollutant dispersion, and urban air mobility. However, its accurate characterization typically requires expensive vertical-profiling LiDAR instruments, which limits the number of locations that can be simultaneously monitored. Building upon previous work in which machine-learning algorithms were trained on LiDAR data from the University of León (Spain) to reconstruct full ABL wind profiles from a single near-surface measurement, this study replaces the traditional data-driven neural network approach with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), embedding a physical constraint directly into the loss function as evaluated by automatic differentiation, and tests two such constraints under architectural control: the Ekman boundary-layer momentum balance, closed with a Monin–Obukhov eddy viscosity, and a shear-constrained formulation based on a power-law profile with an inferred exponent. With dense supervision at the target heights, neither constraint improves on an architecture-matched network without a physical term (RMSE 1.35–1.36 m/s, direction MAE 20.1–20.4∘ across all three, Kruskal–Wallis p=0.0125). In a vertical-extrapolation protocol, training with gates up to 111 m, selecting models by their skill at 140 m, and testing blind on 170–300 m, the Ekman constraint shows no detectable advantage over its own architectural control. In contrast, the shear-constrained model does, reaching 1.80±0.01 m/s speed RMSE and 27.0∘±0.3∘ direction MAE against 2.66±0.10 m/s and 34.2∘±1.8∘ for the Ekman-constrained arm and 2.61±0.12 m/s and 33.9∘±2.0∘ for the physics-free arm, which are statistically indistinguishable from one another; the shear-constrained gain is confirmed against its own architectural control (2.64±0.08 m/s, 33.0∘±1.8∘, matching the physics-free arm), ruling out the additional output as the explanation, and converts an erratic extrapolator into a stable one. The results are consistent with the benefit of embedding physics into the loss being therefore specific to the extrapolation regime and to the formulation tested, not a generic property of physics-informed learning. These findings are based on data from a single suburban site, and multi-site validation remains necessary before they can be generalized. By eliminating the need for continuous LiDAR operation after the training phase, the proposed methodology aims to enable cost-effective monitoring of multiple locations with a single instrument.

title: [Remote Sensing] A Training-Independent Sentinel-1/2 Phenological Approach for Interpretable Paddy Rice Mapping in Heilongjiang, China
abstract: Accurate identification of paddy rice from satellite imagery is challenging in heterogeneous agricultural landscapes because water, wetland, and vigorous summer vegetation can exhibit spectral and radar responses similar to those of rice at individual observation dates. This study develops an interpretable, training-independent rice-mapping approach, meaning that the final classification does not rely on supervised classifier training, although manually interpreted locations were used for exploratory threshold selection. The approach identifies paddy fields from their characteristic transition from early-season inundation to subsequent canopy development. These phenological signals were integrated using explicit decision rules within a cropland-constrained domain, followed by persistent-water exclusion and spatial refinement. The framework was applied to the 2025 rice-growing season in the agricultural regions analyzed in Heilongjiang Province, China, using 30 m output mapping. Validation with 695 independent reference observations yielded an overall accuracy of 92.09%, Cohen’s kappa of 0.791, rice producer’s accuracy of 94.87%, user’s accuracy of 75.90%, and an F1-score of 84.33%. The high producer’s accuracy indicates effective detection of reference rice locations, whereas the lower user’s accuracy shows that commission error remains the principal limitation, particularly in areas with moisture and vegetation conditions resembling paddy fields. Sequential screening further showed that combining phenological evidence with cropland and water constraints substantially reduced the candidate mapping domain. The proposed approach provides an auditable alternative to training-dependent classification workflows and offers a transparent basis for repeatable rice mapping and agricultural monitoring, while requiring further evaluation across multiple years and regions before broader operational transfer.

title: [Remote Sensing] Cross-Scale Consistency and Scale Effects of Vegetation Phenology Across China: Evidence from MODIS Data
abstract: Vegetation phenology derived from satellite vegetation indices is sensitive to spatial scale, yet how spatial aggregation affects phenological timing and temporal dynamics across broad geographical extents remains insufficiently understood. In this study, the 250 m MOD13Q1 Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) time series from 2000 to 2024 was used as a common data source, and 1 km and 5 km datasets were generated directly through spatial aggregation. By maintaining the same sensor, vegetation index, temporal sampling, and phenology retrieval method across scales, this controlled within-source framework minimizes confounding effects associated with cross-sensor differences. The start of the growing season (SOS) and end of the growing season (EOS) were retrieved using asymmetric Gaussian fitting combined with a dynamic threshold method. Their spatiotemporal patterns, aggregation-induced cross-scale consistency, and bias were systematically analyzed. The broad spatial patterns of multi-year mean SOS and EOS remained generally consistent across the three scales. SOS showed an overall advancing tendency and EOS an overall delaying tendency, while the proportion of pixels with relatively large trend magnitudes decreased at coarser spatial scales. Cross-scale correlations remained high across all scale pairs and generally increased with latitude, with SOS exhibiting higher cross-scale consistency than EOS. Annual SOS correlations declined during 2000–2024, whereas EOS correlations increased during the early part of the record and declined thereafter, with a breakpoint around 2010. The bias showed clear differences in direction and magnitude between SOS and EOS and among vegetation types, and its absolute magnitude generally increased with increasing scale disparity. These results indicate that aggregation-induced phenological responses are not spatially uniform but vary systematically with geographical context, vegetation type, and phenological phase. These findings provide a scientific reference for the cross-scale comparison and scale transformation of multi-source remotely sensed phenology products, as well as for studies of regional ecological processes.

title: [Remote Sensing] Cross-Field Transfer of UAV-Based Winter Wheat Yield Prediction: Model Transferability and Sample Efficiency
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing is widely used for plot-scale crop yield prediction, but model performance may decline when models are transferred across fields with different crop, environmental, management, and sensing conditions. This study evaluated the cross-field transferability of UAV-based winter wheat yield models using multispectral (MS), RGB, and thermal infrared (TIR) information. Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models were evaluated under five strategies: target-only training (T1), direct transfer (T2), nitrogen-based adaptation (T3), cultivar-based adaptation (T4), and mixed adaptation (T5). Direct transfer increased the normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) from 12.7% to 14.0% for CatBoost and from 12.9% to 15.9% for MLP. Mixed adaptation achieved the best overall performance, with coefficient of determination (R2) values of 0.84 and 0.87 and NRMSE values of 11.7% and 10.9% for CatBoost and MLP, respectively. After controlling for calibration sample size, the difference between T3 and T4 became smaller, indicating that adaptation performance was influenced by both calibration-data composition and sample availability. CatBoost showed diminishing returns near the 40% calibration level in this experiment, whereas MLP continued to benefit from additional target-domain samples. Prediction errors were higher for samples beyond the source-domain yield range, while mixed adaptation reduced prediction errors in both yield-range groups. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and sensor-level ablation showed that MS features provided important predictive information, while RGB and TIR provided complementary information. These results indicate that target-domain adaptation can improve cross-field UAV yield prediction and highlight the importance of calibration design, yield-range mismatch, and multi-sensor information when transferring models to new fields.

title: [Remote Sensing] High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
abstract: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. Moreover, BA algorithms are typically driven by fire detection products to minimize false identifications. The resulting accuracy of such BA products depends strongly on land cover, fire regime, and the reliability of the considered fire detection products. In this paper, we exploit the multitemporal Robust Satellite Technique (RST) to identify burned areas and implement a workflow based on Sentinel-2 images within Google Earth Engine. Test results from two complete region-wide experiments conducted under contrasting seasonal, phenological, and agricultural conditions showed that 97.85% of the mapped area was confirmed as burned within the adopted multi-source validation framework, with an area-based commission error of 1.38% and omission error of 0.60%. title: [Remote Sensing] LuTan-1 InSAR-Constrained Reconstruction of Concealed Coal-Mining Working-Face Geometry
abstract: To address the difficulty in determining underground working face geometry when mining records are incomplete or mining activities are concealed, this study proposes an InSAR-constrained method for inverting the geometric parameters of concealed working faces. The method uses the line-of-sight (LOS) deformation field derived from LuTan-1 InSAR observations as the primary input. The search ranges of mining depth, mining thickness, coal seam dip angle, strike azimuth, working face center coordinates, strike length, and dip length are constrained using the morphology of the subsidence basin, available empirical parameters, and the Probability Integral Method (PIM). These constraints reduce the uncertainty caused by a large search space and parameter coupling in high-dimensional inversion. An adaptive multi-strategy differential evolution algorithm is then introduced. Latin hypercube sampling is used for population initialization. Dynamic parameter adjustment, multiple mutation strategies, reflective boundary handling, and local refinement are incorporated to improve optimization stability in complex parameter spaces. The simulation results show that the proposed method generally outperforms particle swarm optimization, genetic algorithm, evolutionary strategy, and standard differential evolution in inversion accuracy, convergence stability, and robustness to errors. It can reliably recover the main geometric parameters of a predefined working face. In the engineering case study of the 97,315 working face, the inverted active-mining geometry during the LuTan-1 observation period is generally consistent with the corresponding mine records, with a deformation-fitting RMSE of 32.53 mm and relative errors of the main geometric parameters below 7.9%. Parameter sensitivity analysis further shows that the geometric dimensions and center location of the working face have pronounced effects on the LOS deformation field. These parameters should therefore be tightly constrained during inversion. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a feasible remote-sensing approach for identifying concealed working faces and estimating goaf geometric parameters in mining areas with incomplete records.

title: [Remote Sensing] APFNet: An Adaptive Perception Fusion Network for Multi-Scale Object Detection in Remote Sensing
abstract: Accurate multi-scale object detection remains challenging in remote sensing (RS) imagery due to severe scale variation, limited pixel occupancy of small targets, and complex backgrounds. The Adaptive Perception Fusion Network (APFNet) targets these two aspects through four operations: (1) Split-ELAN (SP-ELAN), a channel-compressed serial refinement backbone whose design is motivated by small-object feature preservation; (2) Adaptive Sampling (AS), which produces sample-dependent channel weights from a global descriptor during cross-scale alignment; (3) Adaptive Gating (AG), which is coupled with AS and aggregates the recalibrated features at complementary receptive-field scales; and (4) Adaptive Context Aggregation (ACA), which aligns three feature levels and applies parallel large-kernel depthwise branches to supply broader multi-scale context. A complete 23 component-group study under one scratch/no-augmentation protocol yields positive conditional contrasts for SP-ELAN, ACA, and the coupled AS–AG pathway. LEVIR and RSOD provide additional cross-dataset and configuration-selection results. These operations use established primitives; the contribution lies in their routing and aggregation.

title: [Remote Sensing] Advanced AI-Based Techniques for Empirical Chronological Mapping of Lava Flows Using Multispectral Satellite Imagery: A Case Study of Mount Etna
abstract: Effusive volcanic eruptions pose significant hazards to populated areas, making the accurate dating of lava flows essential for reconstructing eruptive histories and assessing volcanic risk. Traditional dating techniques, such as radiometric, paleomagnetic and lichenometric methods, are highly reliable but require direct sampling, complex analytical procedures, and substantial financial resources. Satellite remote sensing provides a non-invasive and spatially extensive approach that can complement conventional methods in the regional investigation of exposed volcanic surfaces. This study presents a two-stage hybrid classification–regression framework for empirical age estimation and chronological mapping of historical lava surfaces on Mount Etna, spanning the 17th to the 21st centuries. In the first stage, a Random Forest Classifier distinguishes background, pre-1600 lava surfaces, and post-1600 historical lava surfaces, thereby defining the spatial applicability domain of the chronological model. In the second stage, a Random Forest Regressor estimates age only for pixels classified as post-1600 lava by integrating ten Sentinel-2 surface-reflectance bands, elevation derived from the Digital Elevation Model (DEM), and a binary north-flank spatial indicator. On the balanced pixel-level test dataset, the RFR achieved an R2 of 0.549, a Mean Absolute Error of 66.2 years, and a Root Mean Squared Error of 89.0 years. Using the median prediction for each test eruption, the corresponding eruption-level values were R2=0.701, MAE =51.6 years, and RMSE =67.2 years. Prediction errors were larger for the oldest evaluated surfaces, indicating reduced empirical discrimination near the lower boundary of the calibrated chronological domain. This pattern may reflect calibration-boundary effects, sparse chronological coverage, eruption-specific variability, and possible convergence of surface spectral properties. Comparison with an RBF-SVR showed comparable but metric-dependent performance, without establishing the overall superiority of either regression architecture. Permutation analysis indicated that most predictive information within this dataset was associated with the Sentinel-2 spectral component, particularly the Red Edge bands. The proposed method should therefore be interpreted as a complementary fast empirical lava age-estimation and regional screening framework for exposed historical lava surfaces, rather than as a substitute for radiometric, paleomagnetic, or field-based dating.

title: [Remote Sensing] Non-Linear PSInSAR Analysis of Surface Deformation Using Sentinel-1 Data: Evaluating the Effects of Urban Expansion
abstract: Surface deformation monitoring plays a crucial role in various fields, including geology, geodesy, and environmental studies. This study provides insights into the application of non-linear PSInSAR techniques for studying surface deformation associated with urban growth and groundwater pumping. A Persistent Scatterer InSAR (PSInSAR) analysis employing a time-segmented (non-linear) velocity model was applied to 119 Sentinel-1A ascending acquisitions spanning 10 February 2017 to 27 December 2020, yielding 38,594 persistent scatterers. The 33,238 scatterers were retained at a temporal coherence threshold of 0.70 and a mean density of 18.6 PS/km2 across the district, rising to 57 PS/km2 within the urban core, with annual mean line-of-sight (LOS) velocities measured for each calendar year. Temporal validation identifies a modest, origin-dependent forecasting benefit from segmentation in the urban core but no consistent advantage under contiguous block testing. Land use/land cover (LULC) was mapped from Landsat imagery for 2000, 2007, 2014, and 2020 using a random forest classifier in Google Earth Engine. LOS velocities span approximately +40 to −60 mm/yr over the mapped range, with the most negative values concentrated in the central urban core. Paired annual comparisons, accounting for spatial dependence and Holm adjustment across 15 tests, did not establish significant changes in the 0–2 km core. Significant contrasts occurred in two comparison annuli, but their physical origin remains unresolved. Land use classification maps for the years 2000, 2007, 2014, and 2020 show a significant expansion in built-up areas, coupled with a reduction in vegetation and, after adjustment for classification accuracy, in water bodies, which indicates the increasing pressure of urban growth on the environment. Lahore has witnessed a substantial increase in population due to urban migration, natural growth, and economic opportunities. Subsidence can lead to structural damage to buildings, infrastructure, and underground utilities. It is a serious concern in Lahore, particularly in areas where groundwater pumping is excessive.

title: [Remote Sensing] Automatic Extraction of Discontinuity Traces from Rock Mass Point Cloud Data Using PhaseVote
abstract: Accurate and thorough detection of rock mass discontinuities is essential in geotechnical engineering as they have a significant impact on the stability of underground and surface excavations, yet they are difficult to automate. In the work reported here, an automatic algorithm, termed PhaseVote, is proposed for the extraction of discontinuity traces from the colour (RGB) attributes of 3D meshes which, combined with the region growing method, can help derive more accurate discontinuity modelling of a rock mass. Conventional edge detection methods degrade under low contrast and variable illumination, and geometry-based point-cloud methods overlook spectral features. The proposed approach uses contrast-invariant phase-based feature detection. The detected edges are filtered and then extended or pruned to form major discontinuity traces using the tensor voting method. The first algorithm, phase analysis, detects edges independently of local contrast, while the latter, tensor voting, links and denoises the resultant edge fragments into continuous traces using perceptual grouping. The detection capability of the proposed method is assessed by applying it to two case studies and comparing the results with an existing method. PhaseVote achieved detection rates of 94.85% and 84.72% and IoUs of 70.27% and 69.80%, compared with 76.12%/45.95% and 69.81%/43.81% for a conventional existing method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is resilient to image contrast, robust to changes in the orientation of discontinuity planes, is less subjective and has a higher degree of automation.

title: [Remote Sensing] An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Sentinel-1 SAR Wave-Mode Significant Wave Height Retrieval via Spotter-Buoy-Corrected ERA5 Reanalysis
abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) is a fundamental parameter for ocean engineering, maritime safety, and climate studies. Although spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) wave mode observations provide global, all-weather coverage, accurate SWH retrieval remains challenging due to the complex ocean-to-SAR imaging mechanism. This paper presents an explainable machine learning algorithm for retrieving SWH from Sentinel-1 SAR wave mode data. To address the scarcity of high-quality collocations and the black-box nature of existing deep-learning approaches, we first correct ERA5 SWH against high-quality Spotter drifting in situ using quantile mapping (QM). The bias-corrected ERA5 data are then collocated with Sentinel-1 SAR to generate a large-scale, globally distributed, and Spotter-calibrated training dataset. Here, QM maps each quantile of the ERA5 data distribution onto the corresponding quantile of the collocated Spotter distribution, thereby adjusting the statistical distribution of the reanalysis. An eXtreme gradient boosting regression model is then trained on 32 physically interpretable features extracted from Sentinel-1 Level-2 products, including image statistics, spectral parameters, azimuth cutoff wavelength, normalized radar cross section, and wind-related variables. Comprehensive temporal-independent validations against Spotter buoys and multi-mission altimeter data throughout one year of 2021 (excluded both from the QM correction and from model training) demonstrate high accuracy, with root-mean-square errors of 0.36 m (WV1) and 0.45 (WV2) for SAR–Spotter matchups over the range 0.5–10.0 m. In addition, SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) analysis is employed to quantify feature contributions and enhance model transparency. Furthermore, a compact 12-feature model selected via SHAP-based hierarchical clustering retains a nearly equivalent performance while improving interpretability. The proposed approach offers a reliable and transparent solution for global SAR-based SWH monitoring.

title: [Forests] Fragmented Networks, Detoured Access: A Nationwide Graph-Theoretic Analysis of Forest Road Connectivity in the Republic of Korea
abstract: Forest road networks are almost universally characterised by road density alone, which says nothing about how the roads are arranged. We assembled the 2025 national forest road network of the Republic of Korea (14,007 routes; 25,958 km) with the 1:5000 national road centreline layer into a weighted graph and analysed it with graph-theoretic connectivity indices, centrality and two measures of circuity. Considered alone, the registered forest road system is a disconnected network of 4742 components in which circuitry is close to absent. Public roads bring 96.0% of forest road length into one connected component, almost entirely through minor and unclassified roads, so the system is functionally connected; the quality of that connection is what is measured here. Route-level circuity averaged 1.574 (95% CI 1.568–1.579), whereas the median of the individual circuity ratios between adjacent components was 2.92 (2.82–3.06). The median straight-line gap was 708 m and the median network distance 3002 m, separate medians that need not describe the same pair. Ridge height accounts for part of that variation (Spearman +0.37) but not all of it. Assuming the statutory 10% grade ceiling, the geometrically estimated length of a connecting link was shorter than the existing network path for most adjacent pairs; the estimate is geometric and is not an alignment design. Two-thirds of pairs already lie closer together than half the spacing implied by the national density, so connectivity is a second planning criterion alongside density rather than a substitute for it.

title: [Remote Sensing] Dual-Domain Fusion for Small-Object SAR Ship Detection in Complex Scenes
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ship detection is essential for maritime surveillance, yet coherent speckle can obscure tiny offshore vessels, while high-response coastal structures can produce target-like responses. Repeated downsampling further weakens sparse vessel signatures, whereas a separate high-resolution prediction head increases dense prediction costs. We propose a dual-domain detector that embeds spatial–frequency encoding, multiscale refinement, and high-resolution feature transfer within the backbone–neck–pyramid representation. Scharr-derived boundary cues are coupled with learned frequency context and remain discriminative as features are fused across scales, while sample-preserving space-to-depth transformation and global–local receptive-field modeling integrate shallow detail into semantically stronger P3 features without introducing a separate P2 prediction head. Coordinated FSEM, MSFE, and SOEP modules preserve fine vessel structure and reduce clutter-induced ambiguity throughout the detection hierarchy. Experiments on SSDD, HRSID, and RSDD-SAR evaluate detection accuracy, cross-dataset transfer, limited-data behavior, sensitivity to controlled perturbations, and edge deployment. Across 30 seed-matched SSDD runs, the method improves mAP50:95 over the baseline by 2.70±0.34 percentage points. It achieves 69.3% and 71.5% mAP50:95 on HRSID and RSDD. On the Atlas 200I platform, the compiled FP16 model retains 69.3% mAP50:95 while running at 101.8 frames/s.

title: [Remote Sensing] Shape-Adaptive Learning and Style-Aware Decomposition for Domain-Generalized Oriented Object Detection
abstract: Oriented object detection is essential for interpreting high-resolution remote-sensing images, but detectors trained on a single source domain often suffer from severe performance degradation under unseen imaging conditions. Existing domain generalization methods mainly address horizontal detection or treat style variation as an undifferentiated perturbation, while the geometry-sensitive nature of oriented objects, especially elongated instances, is insufficiently considered. To address these limitations, a shape-adaptive learning and style-aware decomposition framework, termed SA-DGOD, is proposed for single-source domain-generalized oriented object detection. A frozen CLIP image encoder is employed only during training to provide multi-level style statistics, from which several interpretable branch-style pseudo-domains are constructed by modulating feature statistics that characterize photometric and contrast variations. These explicit pseudo-domain identities enable structured style diversification without accessing target-domain data. To improve orientation-sensitive representation learning, a shape-adaptive soft consistency loss is introduced for rotated RoI features. Instead of using a fixed-threshold binary weighting scheme, the proposed loss adopts an aspect-ratio-aware threshold and a continuous rotated-IoU-based weight, allowing elongated objects and geometrically reliable proposals to be handled more flexibly. Furthermore, a style-aware common-specific classifier decomposition is introduced into the proposed framework to separate domain-invariant category discrimination from pseudo-domain-specific style bias. Extensive experiments on multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of SA-DGOD.

title: [Remote Sensing] LiDAR-Assisted Survey Locates Unregistered Rock Shelters in the Blue Mountains, Australia
abstract: Rock shelters are important cultural and archaeological sites in Australia, often containing evidence of Aboriginal occupation and symbolic expression. While rock shelters have been investigated across Australia, locating them in rugged environments through pedestrian surveys remains challenging. This research contributes a methodology which integrates remote sensing, GIS analyses, and archaeological survey to locate rock shelters in the Blue Mountains. We produced models in ArcGIS Pro that analyse high-resolution, UAV-based LiDAR datasets and publicly available, low-resolution, aircraft-based LiDAR datasets from the New South Wales government. Our models yield locations of potential rock shelters, which can be visually evaluated in 3D LiDAR point clouds and ground-truthed through archaeological survey. Ground-truthing confirmed the successful detection of six known rock shelters on UAV and NSW LiDAR datasets, producing more accurate coordinates than the ones listed in online databases. Significantly, we identified three previously unregistered rock shelters that preserve rock art and lithics. These promising results indicate capacity to improve the spatial accuracy of legacy site records and locate unregistered archaeological rock shelters within, and potentially beyond, Australia. Our methodology promotes targeted and efficient survey of rock shelters that can produce regional datasets benefitting local communities, archaeology, and cultural heritage management.

title: [Remote Sensing] CVAC-Net: Cross-View Alignment and Adaptive Collaboration Network for Aerial–Ground Visual Tracking
abstract: Aerial–ground visual tracking facilitates dynamic remote sensing and scene monitoring by integrating complementary observations from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and ground cameras, allowing one view to compensate when the target is poorly observed or temporarily invisible in the other. title: [Remote Sensing] Estimating Downward Shortwave Radiation over Complex Terrain: Synergizing Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Data via Physics-Guided XGBoost
abstract: Downward shortwave radiation (DSR) varies strongly across mountain slopes, and products designed for horizontal surfaces may not resolve this variability. We estimated slope-parallel DSR at eight Saihanba sites using Sentinel-2 imagery, topography, atmospheric inputs, and BRDF-informed surface albedo. Both branches used XGBoost, with the clear-sky branch further incorporating a parameterized radiation anchor, bounded residual learning, and support-aware output correction. On the 2024 test set (n = 1451), the full framework achieved an RMSE of 92.60 W/m2, an NRMSE of 15.79% and an R2 of 0.897. Pooled leave-one-site-out validation across all 6096 samples yielded an RMSE of 113.68 W/m2. For horizontal-surface observations at 10 Heihe River Basin stations, NRMSE was 17.60%. Clear-sky estimates depended most on solar-incidence geometry, whereas top-of-atmosphere spectra dominated the cloudy-sky XGBoost model.

title: [Remote Sensing] Seasonal Prior-Guided Dynamic Forecasting of Nonstationary Gridded PM2.5 Concentrations in China
abstract: Accurate and timely short-term forecasting of gridded PM2.5 concentrations is essential for air-quality management and public health protection, especially for the growing elderly population who are particularly vulnerable to air pollution. Advances in multi-source environmental data and deep learning have substantially improved the spatiotemporal prediction of PM2.5 concentrations. However, existing studies have mainly focused on developing increasingly sophisticated model architectures and optimization strategies while insufficiently considering the temporal nonstationarity of PM2.5 pollution and the recurrent characteristics associated with similar seasonal environmental regimes. Changes in natural environmental conditions and anthropogenic emissions can continuously alter the relationships governing PM2.5 concentrations, challenging the stability of continuous short-term forecasting; meanwhile, historically recurring seasonal pollution characteristics provide potentially valuable prior information for model adaptation. To address this problem, we propose a Seasonal Prior-guided Elastic Weight Consolidation (Seasonal EWC) framework for dynamic forecasting of nonstationary gridded PM2.5 concentrations in China. The framework derives season-specific parameter anchors and Fisher-based parameter importance from historical seasonal conditions and uses this prior knowledge to guide parameter updates during continuous short-term forecasting. Experiments with four representative spatiotemporal forecasting models showed that Seasonal EWC produced architecture-dependent changes in forecasting performance, reducing the annual mean MAE and RMSE by 30.3% and 31.7% for U-Net and by 10.9% and 7.6% for Earthformer, with only small improvements for IAM4VP and mixed changes for ConvLSTM. Parameter analysis revealed that Seasonal EWC reduced parameter-update magnitudes by approximately 27–32% and substantially limited long-term parameter deviation, indicating more stable adaptation during continuous forecasting. These findings demonstrate that seasonal prior knowledge can effectively guide dynamic model adaptation under evolving PM2.5 conditions, providing a promising approach for continuous short-term air-quality forecasting.

title: [Forests] Green Efficiency and Productivity Change in Wood Waste Utilization Across EU Countries: A Directional Distance Function Approach
abstract: Efficient wood waste utilization supports the circular bioeconomy, but comparative evidence on national treatment systems remains limited. This study benchmarks 21 EU member states using radial and non-radial directional distance functions (DDFs), distinguishing pathway-specific adjustment potential. Eurostat data cover seven biennial reporting years from 2010 to 2022 (147 observations). Domestic wood waste generation is the input; material and energy recovery are desirable outputs; landfilling and incineration without energy recovery constitute the undesirable output. Productivity is assessed using a radial Global Malmquist–Luenberger index and an additive non-radial Luenberger indicator. Poland, Germany and France are closest to the non-radial frontier. Spain and Portugal show the largest baseline non-radial scores, dominated by proportional energy-recovery adjustments. Input adjustments are zero in the estimated solutions, but this does not establish independence from waste volume; across the 21 country averages, the association is negative and borderline non-significant at the 5% level (Spearman ρ = −0.43, p = 0.051); the observation-level association (ρ = −0.27, p = 0.001; n = 147) is not independent because it involves repeated observations within countries. Rankings remain similar under an aggregate treatment-volume cap (ρ = 0.96). A generation-normalized direction removes the extreme values and shifts the dominant adjustment towards material recovery. Results identify specification-dependent benchmark gaps rather than physically attainable targets or causal policy prescriptions, supporting pathway-specific monitoring alongside assessments of waste quality and environmental impacts.

title: [Remote Sensing] PRIVER: Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-Scale Visual Evidence Reranking for High-Resolution Remote-Sensing Imagery
abstract: High-resolution remote-sensing images contain dense object layouts and fine spatial details, but their spatial extent makes direct vision–language interpretation difficult. Patch retrieval offers a practical alternative by returning local regions as candidate evidence for downstream interpretation. However, independent semantic scores can leave relevant patches at isolated ranks or return lists with substantial irrelevant content. We propose Prompt-Stable Reciprocal Inter-scale Visual Evidence Reranking (PRIVER), a post-retrieval method for ranking patches within one image using controlled object-category queries. It aggregates four predefined prompt templates and combines semantic scores with geometric support, principally from a degree-normalized inter-scale graph. No encoder weights are updated, and retrieval and reranking do not access object annotations. Parameters are selected on annotated DOTA-v1.5 development data and held fixed. With relevance defined by annotated object coverage, Precision@10 on 458 DOTA-v1.5 internal-test images increases from 0.567 to 0.625 (absolute gain 0.058; 95% source-image cluster bootstrap interval [0.052, 0.065]). Normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank 10 (nDCG@10) increases from 0.647 to 0.730 and distinct-object coverage at rank 10 from 0.773 to 0.873. On a disjoint 526-image SODA-A subset, the corresponding metrics increase from 0.414 to 0.502, 0.445 to 0.550, and 0.467 to 0.681. Coverage-based gains persist with GeoRSCLIP and RemoteCLIP and under altered tiling policies on fixed image subsets. Inter-scale support is the principal source of improvement. These results support training-free, coverage-defined patch prioritization for within-image visual evidence retrieval.

title: [Remote Sensing] Reference Data Generation for Remote Sensing Image Classification: A Comprehensive Review of Methods, Challenges, and Recent Advances
abstract: Image classification is a fundamental technique that has been broadly adopted in remote sensing, computer vision and related areas. High-quality annotated datasets are necessary for the development and reliable evaluation of classification and segmentation algorithms for accurate thematic mapping. Reference data are critical in this sense, as their quality has a direct impact on the performance, accuracy and generalization of the model. However, generating reliable reference data remains challenging due to methodological, technical, and annotation-related uncertainties. This study reviews the principal challenges in reference data generation, and the solutions proposed in scientific literature. A total of 100 papers indexed in the Web of Science were examined. The review covers traditional reference data generation methods as well as emerging approaches based on semi-supervised, self-supervised, and active learning, segmentation- and post-processing-assisted labeling, benchmark dataset construction, sampling and accuracy assessment, and deep learning and automated label generation. Major challenges and emerging research directions are also discussed. The results indicate a clear shift from traditional manual techniques to more automated, learning based and accuracy driven methods. The study provides a framework of existing techniques and future research areas in image classification.

title: [Remote Sensing] Enhanced Quantitative Precipitation Estimation During Typhoon Storms Based on Optimized Dual-Polarimetric Radar Quality Control
abstract: Accurate radar-based quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) plays a critical role in disaster prevention and reduction. In mountainous terrain, blockage of low-elevation radar beams can lead to missing low-level precipitation observations, while errors in specific differential phase KDP retrieval further limit QPE accuracy. To address these issues, this study uses data from two S-band dual-polarization weather radars located in Fangchenggang and Beihai, together with ground rain gauges, local raindrop size distribution (DSD) data, and digital elevation model (DEM) data. Hybrid-scan elevation construction and dual-radar mosaicking are adopted to improve the effective coverage of low-elevation observations, and a threshold-fusion strategy for KDP, denoted as KDP_TF, is proposed. The strategy selects the larger of the conventionally quality-controlled KDP_QC and variationally reconstructed KDP_VR at each valid gate. Based on the CSU-HIDRO algorithm, three QPE products, namely the quality-control QPE (QC_QPE), the variational-reconstruction QPE (VR_QPE), and the threshold-fusion QPE (TF_QPE), are generated. The precipitation events associated with Typhoon Yagi in 2024 and Typhoon Matmo in 2025 are selected for evaluation. The results indicate that TF_QPE most effectively mitigates the underestimation of 24 h accumulated precipitation. Compared with QC_QPE, the magnitude of the negative relative bias (RB) of TF_QPE is reduced, from −27.30% to −20.07% and from −16.56% to −9.78%, respectively, for the Yagi and Matmo events; the root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases from 46.76 to 43.79 mm and from 43.27 to 43.13 mm, respectively. The hourly precipitation results further show that TF_QPE better captures the peak intensity of heavy precipitation and exhibits no evident temporal lag relative to rain gauge observations. For the heavy precipitation category, TF_QPE also yields the highest probability of detection (POD) and critical success index (CSI). These results suggest that the QPE framework developed in this study, which integrates hybrid-scan elevation construction, dual-radar mosaicking, and threshold-fusion-based KDP optimization, can improve the effective low-elevation observational coverage in mountainous terrain and mitigate the underestimation of typhoon-induced heavy precipitation in radar QPE. These results provide technical references for typhoon-related heavy-rainfall monitoring and flood early-warning as well as radar-QPE applications over coastal Guangxi.

title: [Remote Sensing] Adaptive Timing of Landslide Susceptibility Map Updates Using Persistent Deformation Changes
abstract: Interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) provides spatially extensive deformation measurements that support dynamic landslide susceptibility assessment. However, determining when landslide susceptibility maps require updating remains insufficiently studied. Here, we introduce the persistent deformation-change area ratio (PDAR), the percentage of monitored slope-unit area exhibiting persistent velocity changes relative to each unit’s accepted reference. Three-observation confirmation and reference resetting allow update intervals to respond to both increasing and decreasing deformation. A common asymmetric matrix combines the current susceptibility class with the relative velocity change, allowing at most two upward steps or one downward step. We compared PDAR with no updating and fixed one-, three-, six- and twelve-month schedules across 6956 slope units in Yunyang, Kaizhou and Wushan. Baseline construction used 2013–2016, parameter calibration used 2017–2018, and evaluation covered 2019–2022. PDAR achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC; 0.7913 versus 0.6848 without updating), highest high/very high event capture (63.99%) and lowest false-positive rate (FPR; 13.67%). Relative to monthly updating, AUC increased by 0.1162 and FPR decreased by 12.92 percentage points. PDAR also exceeded the strongest fixed schedule, six-month updating, by 0.0688 in AUC. The fixed-window comparison showed that more frequent updating was not always beneficial. PDAR provides a state-dependent basis for selecting update windows rather than updating whenever newer observations become available.

title: [Remote Sensing] DAMD-Net: Anisotropic Range–Doppler Feature Learning for Maritime Target Recognition
abstract: Range–Doppler (RD) spectrogram-based maritime target recognition requires effective feature learning when labeled training samples are limited and the range and Doppler axes convey different physical information. We propose DAMD-Net, which combines Asymmetric Dimension-Aware Fusion (ADF) with a Dual-Directional Attention Module (DDAM). ADF integrates range-wise scattering features, Doppler-wise motion features, and local two-dimensional context, while DDAM recalibrates the fused representation through axis-specific descriptors and learnable fusion weights. With 5% of the simulated dataset used for training, DAMD-Net achieves 86.15±0.43% accuracy and 83.57±0.41% macro-F1. With 10% used for training, the corresponding results are 89.55±0.39% accuracy and 87.48±0.51% macro-F1. At the smaller 1% and 2% training budgets, DAMD-Net improves macro-F1 over VGG16 by 1.64 and 1.82 percentage points, respectively, with positive unadjusted 95% paired confidence intervals. Each training budget uses an additional 4049 labeled validation samples. Component ablations, kernel and pooling sensitivity studies, and condition-holdout evaluations examine the contribution of directional modeling; DAMD-Net has higher mean accuracy than VGG16 in all three elevation-holdout intervals. Controlled perturbation tests show advantages under partial Doppler masking and structured synthetic clutter: at a baseline-RD-to-added-clutter ratio of −10 dB, accuracy reaches 62.74%, compared with 36.68% for VGG16. On the external MTDSP dataset, DAMD-Net achieves 97.13% accuracy; on the measured LSS-DAUR dataset, it achieves 75.00±14.03% accuracy under five-fold cross-validation. DAMD-Net also reduces parameters by 89.9% and registered FLOPs by 52.6% relative to VGG16. Together, these findings support explicit RD anisotropy modeling for recognition with restricted training data, with complementary benefits in the evaluated disturbance conditions and model storage.

abstract: Object detection in remote sensing scenarios faces multiple challenges, primarily manifested in multi-scale objects, class imbalance, densely packed small targets, and occlusion. To address these issues, we propose DCA-Net, an object detection method based on deep context aggregation. Built upon the YOLO architecture, the proposed method introduces parallel multi-branch pooling paths and an adaptive feature reweighting mechanism to construct a deep context aggregation backbone (DCA-Backbone). title: [Remote Sensing] Assessing Spatio-Temporal Patterns and Statistical Associations of Meteorological and Agricultural Droughts in Winter Wheat Using Multi-Source Data
abstract: Characterizing the spatiotemporal differences between meteorological and agricultural drought is important for drought monitoring and risk management in major grain-producing regions. However, coordinated assessment of meteorological anomalies and crop moisture responses using multi-source data remains challenging. The standardized precipitation index (SPI) and vegetation water index (VWI) were used to characterize meteorological and agricultural drought, respectively. Furthermore, standard deviational ellipse analysis and center-based spatial statistics were used to characterize drought distribution, orientation, and spatial migration, while Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine statistical associations among SPI-defined drought, VWI-defined drought, and effective irrigated area. Across the selected study periods, meteorological and agricultural drought showed distinct temporal and spatial patterns. In addition, the SPI–VWI association varied with drought severity: light drought showed the strongest positive association (r = 0.64), moderate drought showed a weak negative association (r = −0.20), and severe drought showed a moderate positive association (r = 0.57). The association between total SPI- and VWI-defined drought areas was weak (r = −0.07). title: [Remote Sensing] Soil Moisture Retrieval from Sentinel-1 SAR in Arid Oasis Regions: Error Analysis and Incidence Angle Effects
abstract: High-precision inversion of soil moisture content using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data still faces significant technical challenges, as the radar backscatter coefficient is influenced by complex interactions among surface roughness, vegetation cover, and soil permittivity. Therefore, systematically evaluating the mechanisms by which SAR system parameters and surface environmental variables influence soil moisture inversion is of critical scientific importance. This study utilized an improved alpha approximation algorithm in conjunction with Sentinel-1 SAR data to estimate soil moisture content for different land cover types in middle reaches of the Heihe River Basin and analyzed the sources of error in the soil moisture estimation process. The results indicate that the improved alpha approximation algorithm can achieve relatively satisfactory soil moisture inversion results. However, significant differences in the inversion results were still observed under different orbital and incidence angle conditions, with an average RMSE of 0.034 for ascending orbits and 0.037 for descending orbits. In desert regions, data from Ascending Orbit 128 with an incidence angle of 33° yielded the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE, 0.030 m3/m3) and the highest determination coefficient (R2, 0.848). In agricultural areas, the minimum RMSE for 2017 and 2018 was 0.030 m3/m3 and 0.041 m3/m3, respectively, while the maximum R2 values were 0.815 and 0.728, respectively; Compared with the desert region, the accuracy of soil moisture inversion in the agricultural region was reduced due to the influence of vegetation phenology and irrigation activities. Overall, the soil moisture inversion results for both study areas agreed well with field observations but still exhibited significant seasonal and interannual variations. The angle of incidence, surface roughness, vegetation dynamics, precipitation conditions, and irrigation activities were the primary factors affecting the accuracy of soil moisture inversion. Especially, the impact of the static roughness assumption on the accuracy of the alpha approximation algorithm is more pronounced.

title: [Remote Sensing] Joint Super-Resolution and Weighted Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition for Ground Penetrating Radar Clutter Suppression
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is an important non-destructive sensing technology for subsurface detection. However, strong clutter from surface reflection and heterogeneous media often masks weak target responses in B-scan images. Existing low-rank and sparse decomposition (LRSD) methods, such as Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA), can separate clutter and targets but suffer from uniform singular value shrinkage and high computational cost; more critically, they operate only at the original resolution, refining only the spatial sampling grid of the migrated image under the inherent physical resolution limit. In this paper, we propose a Joint Super-Resolution and Weighted Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition (JSR-LRSD) framework that synergistically suppresses clutter and improves the spatial detail and target localization of the migrated image without extending its physical resolution. Unlike cascade approaches, which perform clutter removal first and super-resolution afterward and may amplify residual clutter, our method integrates a differentiable super-resolution network directly into the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) iterations. This allows for the sparse target matrix to be regularized by high-resolution image priors, while the high-resolution estimate adaptively adjusts the weighted nuclear norm via total variation feedback. An adaptive weighted nuclear norm is designed using singular values of the observed data and the total variation feedback from the high-resolution target estimate. A randomized singular value decomposition (SVD) is introduced to accelerate computation. Extensive experiments on simulated and laboratory GPR data demonstrate that the proposed JSR-LRSD achieves a higher signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) compared to conventional and LRSD-based methods, with clear improvement in spatial detail recovery, while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: [Remote Sensing] Groundwater Recovery and Land Deformation in the Beijing Plain: A Review
abstract: Groundwater recovery can reduce land subsidence without immediately reversing aquifer-system compaction. This review synthesizes 101 original studies of the Beijing Plain to examine deformation during groundwater depletion and subsequent recovery. The evidence includes interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR), leveling, groundwater records, borehole deformation measurements and laboratory experiments. Historical surveys and satellite observations document expanding subsidence centers followed by widespread deceleration and localized rebound. Groundwater pressure changes are the principal regional forcing. Sedimentary architecture, hydraulic connectivity and loading history govern the magnitude and timing of deformation. Delayed pressure equilibration and time-dependent strain can sustain compaction after aquifer heads rise, while irreversible strain limits recovery of lost elevation. Surface uplift can therefore coexist with compaction at depth and does not establish restoration of aquifer-system storage capacity. Observational coverage remains uneven: 75 studies use InSAR, whereas 17 report borehole deformation measurements. Paired pressure and interval-deformation measurements are needed to identify the sources of continuing compaction. Differential ground movement remains relevant to infrastructure assessment even where regional subsidence slows.

title: [Remote Sensing] Multi-Index Remote Sensing Assessment of Agro-Climatic Change and Agricultural Responses in Temperate and Semi-Arid Regions
abstract: Diverse climatic regions exhibit unique agro-climatic vulnerabilities that are significantly shaped by climate stress. Understanding these distinct vulnerabilities is essential for developing effective policies to mitigate climate change impacts and ensuring sustainable environmental management. This study examines agro-climatic vulnerabilities in Nottinghamshire County (United Kingdom) and Udaipur District (India) from 2000 to 2024, comparing climate change impacts across temperate and semi-arid agricultural systems that represent fundamentally different system behaviours under contrasting climatic conditions. Using multi-temporal Landsat imagery and WorldClim climate data, nine environmental indices were analysed: the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Vegetation Condition Index (VCI), Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Moisture Stress Index (MSI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Temperature Condition Index (TCI), Vegetation Health Index (VHI), Drought Risk Index (DRI), and Crop Health Index (CHI). The results reveal contrasting regional trajectories that challenge conventional assumptions about climate vulnerability. Udaipur exhibited improved vegetation and moisture conditions across the observation period, whereas Nottinghamshire showed intensifying moisture stress and declining precipitation. Warming was more pronounced in Nottinghamshire, while strong inter-index correlations validated the monitoring approach. These findings indicate that Udaipur benefits from intensified monsoon patterns, requiring flood mitigation and water-storage infrastructure, whereas Nottinghamshire’s rising moisture stress underscores the need for sustained monitoring and adaptive management. This comparative framework provides evidence-based insights for region-specific adaptation strategies essential to sustainable agricultural development across diverse agro-climatic zones.

title: [Remote Sensing] Continuous Radar QPE Bias Field Reconstruction Through the Implicit Neural Representation Framework: QPE-BiasINR
abstract: Biases in high-spatiotemporal-resolution radar quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) can substantially compromise the reliability of meteorological and hydrological disaster warning. Existing QPE correction methods commonly assume predefined spatial smoothness, whereas localized biases can vary sharply over short spatial distances. We therefore propose an implicit neural representation (INR) framework for continuous radar QPE bias-field reconstruction (QPE-BiasINR). QPE-BiasINR introduces QPE-background modulation, which conditions bias estimation on the local precipitation context to account for precipitation-dependent spatial variations in radar QPE errors. Moreover, a multiscale spatial consistency (MSC) constraint is incorporated into the loss function to explicitly strengthen spatial consistency. QPE-BiasINR was evaluated using hourly multi-radar mosaic QPE and gauge observations within the coverage of four radars in the Daqing River Basin,China, during June–September 2023. Test set performance was benchmarked against the uncorrected radar QPE, mean-field bias correction, and Kriging. QPE-BiasINR achieved the highest correlation coefficient (0.84) and the lowest root mean square error (3.29 mm) and mean absolute error (1.68 mm). Ablation experiments on QPE-BiasINR demonstrated that QPE-background modulation improved accuracy, while the MSC constraint reduced localized overcorrection. These results indicate that QPE-BiasINR can improve high-resolution radar QPE, with potential value for hydrological modeling and operational flood-risk monitoring.

title: [Remote Sensing] A Deep Learning Framework for Nonparametric SAR Autofocus Using a Hybrid Architecture
abstract: Autofocus plays a pivotal role in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging, which is particularly crucial for high-resolution applications. Traditional autofocus methods face inherent limitations, such as reliance on strong isolated scatterers within the scene or prohibitive computational complexity, making them inadequate for the practical demands of the rapid and batch processing of massive SAR imagery. Although recent deep learning (DL)-based methods have improved focusing efficiency, they predominantly rely on predefined high-order polynomial models for phase error estimation, which inevitably introduces parameter redundancy, restricts the model’s adaptability to complex phase errors, and is highly prone to inducing severe oscillations at the aperture boundaries. To overcome these limitations, this article proposes DeepAutofocus, a non-parametric deep learning framework for SAR autofocus. First, we design a physics-inspired subaperture correlation Transformer architecture. A multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) is utilized to extract local spatial features, which are then transformed into serialized subaperture image patches. Subsequently, the self-attention mechanism of the Transformer is employed to capture the long-range dependencies across subapertures. Second, we introduce a data-driven cubic B-spline reconstruction strategy that directly estimates phase errors without depending on predefined high-order polynomial models, thereby eliminating boundary oscillations while maintaining high flexibility. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real measured satellite datasets demonstrate that, compared to traditional autofocus algorithms and existing DL-based methods, the proposed DeepAutofocus achieves superior focusing performance under various complex phase error conditions.

title: [Remote Sensing] Susceptibility Zoning of Seasonal Freeze–Thaw Deformation in Permafrost Subgrade Along the Qinghai–Tibet Highway
abstract: Permafrost subgrades along the Qinghai–Tibet Highway exhibit pronounced spatial variability in seasonal freeze–thaw deformation under the combined effects of complex permafrost conditions, climate change, and engineering disturbances. Focusing on the Xidatan–Tuojula Mountains section, this study integrated field monitoring, borehole investigations, subgrade geometric parameters, and multisource remote sensing data to establish a coupled ground–atmosphere model. The maximum refreezing depth (Hf) was selected as the susceptibility indicator, and an extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model based on 172 numerical simulations was developed to predict the spatial distribution of seasonal freeze–thaw deformation susceptibility at a 30 m resolution. The predicted susceptibility index was classified into five levels using the Jenks natural breaks method. The results show that susceptibility along the 532.20 km investigated section exhibits significant spatial heterogeneity. Level I sections account for the largest proportion (30.64%), followed by Level II (18.52%), Level IV (15.40%), Level V (9.54%), and Level III (7.92%). High-susceptibility sections are mainly concentrated in Hoh Xil, Wudaoliang, the Fenghuo Mountains, and the Tanggula Mountains, whereas low-susceptibility sections are primarily distributed in the Tuotuo River Basin, Tongtian River Basin, Wenquan Basin, and the Tuojula Mountains section. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified mean annual ground temperature (MAGT), subgrade height (SH), and ice content type (ICT) as the dominant controlling factors, contributing 51.59%, 26.56%, and 18.16%, respectively. The interactions between MAGT × SH and MAGT × ICT were identified as the dominant two-way interactions. These findings provide insights for identifying critical sections, optimizing monitoring strategies, and supporting zonation-based maintenance of permafrost highways.

title: [Remote Sensing] Multisensor Analysis of Mediterranean Convective Case Studies Using EarthCARE and Meteosat Rapid Scan Observations
abstract: Convection plays a key role in the Earth’s energy balance and is responsible for severe weather phenomena such as hailstorms, which cause significant damage to infrastructure and agriculture. This study investigates convective events over the Mediterranean Basin between September 2024 and September 2025 using a synergistic combination of active and passive satellite observations from geostationary (GEO) and low Earth orbit (LEO) platforms. Convective evolution is analyzed using EUMETSAT Satellite Application Facility on Support to Nowcasting and Very Short Range Forecasting products derived from Meteosat Rapid Scan Service imagery and the Multi-sensor Approach for Satellite Hail Advection (MASHA), which combines passive microwave hail probability retrievals from the Global Precipitation Measurement constellation with high-temporal-resolution Meteosat infrared observations to monitor hail-producing storms in near real time. The analysis is further enhanced with EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar reflectivity and Doppler velocity measurements, whose spatial variability provides a proxy for identifying convective cores and storm intensity. For selected events, observations from the Meteosat Third Generation Lightning Imager are also examined, highlighting the close relationship between intense lightning activity and strong convective updrafts. The results demonstrate the potential of combining complementary satellite observations to improve the detection and characterization of severe convection and hail-producing storms and identify the key roadblocks and pathways towards the effective integration of LEO and GEO observations.

title: [Forests] Knowledge Domains and Practice Orientation in Forestry-Related Research
abstract: Forestry research produces different kinds of knowledge, including ecological explanations, resource assessments, decision tools, and policy analyses, yet its practical content is usually judged by the recommendations it contains. Drawing on full-text articles, this study examines how these kinds of knowledge are connected to practice and how an article’s practical claims appear in its abstract. Five hundred Web of Science articles from 2020 to 2025 were sampled, 100 in each of five knowledge domains. Their concluding material and abstracts were coded separately for practice orientation as scholarly exposition, general applied relevance, or explicit prescription. The domains differed in form as well as the degree of practical relevance. Explicit prescription was most frequent in economics, policy and governance, and in ecology and conservation. Inventory and assessment concentrated on general applied relevance, stated through measurement and mapping output. When the concluding material prescribed, the abstract kept the prescription in 94 of 183 articles and restated it as general relevance in 75. In every domain, at least a third of these prescriptions were not kept in the abstract. Recommendation counts therefore favor domains that prescribe, and abstract-based screening misses much of what conclusions recommend. Through this paired coding, the study offers a domain-sensitive basis for judging practical relevance and measures how much practical guidance abstracts leave out.

title: [Remote Sensing] Geodetic Deformation Inversion of Groundwater Variations in the Golmud River Basin, Northwestern China
abstract: The Golmud River Basin is a typical inland arid river basin in the Qaidam Basin, and the dynamics of its groundwater storage are of great importance for regional ecological security and water resources management. To address the limited spatial representativeness of traditional hydrological station networks and the relatively low spatial resolution of satellite gravimetry such as the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE), this study develops a multi-source geodetic inversion framework for groundwater estimation by using Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), and GRACE satellite gravimetry. Surface deformation with high spatial resolution over the Golmud River Basin is derived from Sentinel-1 SAR images from 2017 to 2021. After correcting for modeled non-hydrological loading effects and screening observations to reduce the influence of potential non-hydrological signals, groundwater spatiotemporal variations are inverted based on elastic loading theory. The results show that from 2017 to 2021, surface deformation in the Golmud River Basin is jointly controlled by river dynamics, mineral extraction, and urbanization, forming a spatial pattern of river corridor zones and mining-related patches. Groundwater storage shows an overall increasing trend during the study period, with a particularly significant increase in the southwestern region, reaching more than 20 mm/a. A synthetic experiment demonstrates that the proposed method can recover prescribed groundwater signals at a spatial resolution of approximately 40 km under the tested conditions. Compared with the InSAR-derived estimates, GRACE-derived groundwater variations exhibit a smaller seasonal amplitude, potentially reflecting the effects of limited spatial resolution and spatial signal smoothing. The WaterGAP Global Hydrology Model (WGHM) estimates are substantially smaller in magnitude than those derived from InSAR and GRACE, highlighting the uncertainties associated with model-based groundwater estimates in this high-altitude basin. Groundwater in the Golmud River Basin experienced a rapid increase during 2017 to 2019, which is likely driven by increased precipitation and lower temperatures associated with a La Niña event, indicating a teleconnection between global climate variability and regional water resource changes. This study provides a technical reference for refined groundwater monitoring at a tens-of-kilometers scale in small and medium-scale arid basin systems.

title: [Remote Sensing] Validation of Satellite-Derived and Reanalysis Solar Irradiance Databases Across Indonesia’s Tropical Climate Zones
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance data are essential for photovoltaic (PV) resource assessment in Indonesia, yet no hourly-resolution multi-database validation exists across the archipelago scale. This study evaluates four gridded solar irradiance databases, CAMS, JAXA Himawari-9, NASA POWER, and ERA5, against quality-controlled ground measurements from 26 BMKG stations spanning all three major Köppen climate zones (Af, Am, Aw) during 2023–2024. CAMS achieved the highest hourly correspondence (median R2 = 0.855, rRMSE = 28.1%), and JAXA was close behind (R2 = 0.848), while NASA POWER showed the lowest systematic bias (rMBE = +3.6%). ERA5 showed the largest hourly errors (R2 = 0.617, rRMSE = 41.2%) consistent with its model-generated cloud fields that are unable to reproduce the localized convective-cloud variability. Because CAMS and JAXA infer cloud from the same Himawari-9 AHI observations on a common 0.05° grid, their comparison reduced sensor and resolution-related differences and focused on the retrieval design. Both showed closely comparable performance (clear-sky R2 = 0.925 vs. 0.913), and this gap widens as cloud frequency increases across the three climate zones. All four databases showed substantially larger relative errors under overcast conditions (Kt < 0.35); the temporal aggregation reduced relative error substantially, with CAMS showing the lowest error at hourly and daily scales and NASA POWER the lowest monthly rRMSE. These results provide an archipelago-scale hourly-resolution validation of four structurally distinct databases across Indonesia’s three tropical climate zones, supporting product selection and bias-correction strategies for solar resource application in Indonesia.

title: [Remote Sensing] MCI-DETR: A Multi-Level Context Interaction Transformer for Small-Object Detection in UAV Imagery
abstract: Small objects in UAV imagery often exhibit weak visual representations, suffer from background clutter, and receive insufficient cross-scale feature interaction. To address these challenges, we develop MCI-DETR, a multi-level contextual interaction detector built upon RT-DETR. First, a Local-Context Modulated Interaction Module (LCMI) is designed to selectively modulate contextual features using local structural responses, thereby suppressing irrelevant background responses while expanding the effective receptive field. Second, CATM is incorporated into the high-level feature interaction stage to form a Context Interaction Module (CCIM), strengthening target-related information through spatial- and channel-domain context mapping and additive Query–Key interaction and reducing the interference of complex backgrounds with the high-level semantic representation of weak small objects. Finally, a Multi-Scale Adaptive Gated Fusion Module (MSAGF) is designed to dynamically adjust the fusion contributions of information at different scales according to the input features, while improving the quality of cross-scale feature fusion through gated coordination between local details and global context. On VisDrone2019, MCI-DETR surpasses RT-DETR by 5.2%, 4.8%, and 3.2% in mAP50, mAP50-95, and APS, respectively, demonstrating enhanced robustness for small-object recognition in cluttered aerial imagery. MCI-DETR also achieves competitive performance on UAVDT and HIT-UAV against representative detectors, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed design under different UAV scenes and imaging conditions. Overall, MCI-DETR strengthens the representation of small objects in aerial scenes and maintains reliable detection performance in the presence of cluttered backgrounds.
